title: Workspace circuits and cost rails — consolidated IA prototype
creator: Aisha Kollins
description: Problem: The Redwood Console currently exposes dashboards, rollout controls, and cost analytics across multiple entry points. Users report confusion when switching workspaces or locating cost breakdowns versus deployment rollouts. Goal: Propose a refreshed information architecture that groups operational surfaces into coherent 'workspace circuits' (contextual lane for most-frequent flows) and 'cost rails' (persistent, discoverable cost lenses), reduces top-level navigation items, standardizes workspace switching, and surfaces rollout state and canary controls near related dashboards. Deliverables: - Figma prototype (three fidelity states): collapsed rail, expanded workspace lens, and cost-drill popover. - Annotated IA map and navigation rules (keyboard paths, deep links). - Usability test plan + 6 moderated sessions. - Handoff package for engineering with route map, a11y checklist, and tokenization examples for cost drilldown APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Single top-level nav with no more than 6 persistent items (Core, Workspaces, Deployments, Observability, Costs, Settings)
Workspace switcher accessible from header and rails; preserves pinned dashboards per workspace
Cost view accessible as a persistent rail state and as a drilldown from dashboard cards
Rollout controls (canary, rollback, traffic split) discoverable from Deployments + contextual dashboard
Prototype validated with 6 users showing >=80% success rate on: switching workspace + finding cost-for-feature, initiating canary rollout
updates: 2025-02-12 — Kickoff: scoped IA problems with PM and Eng; agreed success metrics and user personas (Platform Engineer, Product PM, Growth PM).
2025-02-18 — Low-fidelity sketches posted; explored 3 variants for workspace switcher: global modal, inline flyout, persistent mini-rail. Leaned toward persistent mini-rail for low friction.
2025-02-24 — Figma prototype v1 created (collapsed rail + expanded workspace lens). Shared with ENG and PM for initial feedback. Added keyboard nav flows and deep link examples.

2025-02-26 — Design review with PM (Jin Park) and ENG lead (Sofia Patel): key feedback — (1) Preserve per-workspace pinned dashboards; (2) Cost drilldowns must map cleanly to existing billing APIs to avoid extra backend work; (3) Rollouts should be surfaced under new 'Deployments' top-level item rather than buried in Observability.

2025-02-28 — Updated prototype to include a cost-rail pill that expands to token-level drilldown and connects to existing /costs endpoint patterns. Noted edge case: cross-workspace cost aggregation (requires PM decision).
2025-03-02 — Accessibility pass: contrast checks and tab order adjusted; added aria-live region for rollout state changes. Assigned a11y QA to Riley Chen.

2025-03-04 — Design review v2: Visual polish applied; PM approved roadmap for feature gating (Costs-first for Hosted API, Deployments-first for Dedicated customers). Action: run 6 moderated usability sessions starting 2025-03-09.
Next steps: schedule usability tests, finalize handoff doc, open ENG tickets for route changes (see dependencies).
usability_plan: Recruit 6 participants: 2 Platform Engineers, 2 Product PMs, 2 Growth PMs
Task 1: Switch to a different workspace and pin a dashboard (measure time and errors)
Task 2: Find cost for a specific feature and open token-level drilldown
Task 3: Start a canary rollout and verify rollback option is visible
Success criteria: >80% task completion, median time under 90s for tasks 1 and 2
notes_for_engineering: Routes: propose /workspaces/:id/(dashboards|deployments|costs) to standardize deep links
Keep top-level nav items to 6 for mobile-first collapse behavior
Expose api parameter cost.group_by=feature|model|token for drilldowns
Provide fallback when billing scope is cross-workspace (show aggregated view with warning)
Rollout controls must call existing deployments service v2; if endpoint changes are required, flag for eng backlog
